content:
Para diagnosticar problemas en Thunderbird, prueba una de las siguientes soluciones:

  • Reinicia Thunderbird con los complementos desactivados (Modo seguro TB). En el menú Ayuda, haz clic en "Modo de resolución de problemas" - no uses la casilla de verificación para desactivar permanentemente los complementos. Si Thunderbird se comporta correctamente, puede que un complemento o tema esté interfiriendo con el funcionamiento normal. Para probar:
    • Reinicia Thunderbird y prueba los complementos desactivándolos todos y, a continuación, vuelve a activarlos de uno en uno hasta que localices el que causa el problema. (O si tienes muchos complementos, prueba a desactivar la mitad cada vez).
    • Prueba otros temas.

Si lo anterior no soluciona el problema, una configuración o personalización del usuario podría estar interfiriendo.

  • Reinicia el sistema operativo en modo seguro con funciones de red. Esto carga solo lo básico necesario para iniciar tu ordenador mientras habilita una conexión a Internet. Haz clic en tu sistema operativo para obtener instrucciones sobre cómo iniciar en modo seguro: Windows 11, Windows 10, Windows 8, Windows 7, OSX. (Información general sobre Modo a prueba de fallos.)
Si el modo seguro para el sistema operativo soluciona el problema, entonces el software que se carga durante el inicio del ordenador está causando problemas. Las posibilidades incluyen, entre otras: escaneo de antivirus, virus/malware, descargas en segundo plano como actualizaciones de programas.
  • Si el problema es de rendimiento, sigue los pasos en Perfilado del rendimiento de Thunderbird y proporciónanos una URL a un perfil de rendimiento.

> Was on version 115, had this problem. Updated to version 155, same problem.

I'm not understanding when the problem you are having happened. The above makes it sound like you had the problem on 115 (maybe a couple years ago?) and you still have the problem on 155 (now). But later you say

> This has worked OK until now.

So I'm not understanding on which TB version you first saw the issue. Was it a version before 115 where it worked the way you want it to?

Anyhow, if you can't get into your TB server settings to check the accounts, I think you will need to disable checking for mail at startup. However, I think you are saying you can't get to them due to the error pop-ups. So I think you going to have to disable checking for new mail at startup and checking for new mail every X seconds by (carefully!) edit the prefs.js file in your profile. (I'm assuming you know where to find you profile for now.) With with TB shutdown, open prefs.js in an editor. Find the group of items that start with "mail.server.serverX" where X is the index number for your problem accounts/servers, i.e., the gmail account doing the filtering and and different X value for the other account which "doesn't have a server". In both of these set user_pref("mail.server.serverX.check_new_mail", false);" and, if it exists set "user_pref("mail.server.serverX.check_time", 1000);" or you can just delete the full "check_time" line. Doing this will prevent new mail from being polled for at TB startup on these two accounts. It will also prevent new mail from being checked on a timed basis if you delete the full "time_check" line or it will check it after 1000 minutes so you have plenty of time to check the setting after you start TB before you get the lock-up (or crash as you called it).

Again, if you do this be careful editing the pref.js file and ONLY WITH TB SHUTDOWN. It's suggested to create a user.js file in your profile along side prefs.js with these changes so you might try that first before directly editing prefs.js. But you still need to determine the "X" value for you two problem servers by looking in prefs.js. (Note also, I'm assuming you can't getting into Config Editor when you run TB, which is the best way to change these prefs.)

If after you do this and can go into server setting for the two POP3 accounts, please post your exact setting for both servers (including any "advanced" setting). As Matt pointed out, I don't know how you ever configured a "blank or empty" server name for an account.

If any one reading this thinks they would appreciate some additional help moving from old to new computer:

On OLD computer

  • Exit Thunderbird
  • Access Profile via the following method:
  • In windows search type: %Appdata% - see image as guide
  • Select %Appdata% file folder
  • Click on 'Roaming'
  • Copy the 'Thunderbird' folder to an external drive

On New computer

  • Exit Thunderbird
  • Access Profile via the following method:
  • In windows search type: %Appdata% - see image as guide
  • Select %Appdata% file folder
  • Click on 'Roaming'
  • Delete the 'Thunderbird' folder - it got created by default.
  • On external drive - Copy the 'Thunderbird' folder which came from the OLD computer.
  • Paste the copied 'Thunderbird' folder into the 'Roaming' Folder.

start Thunderbird.

Please note: This info is assuming you got the Thunderbird program download and installation from the official website at this link: https://www.thunderbird.net/en-US/thunderbird/all/ This would create an initial new profile. Everything to do with Thunderbird profiles is in this Thunderbird folder Basically : C: //Users/Username/Appdata/Roaming/Thunderbird.

If you used the Thunderbird installed from the 'Windows App Store' then it create the default profiles in an entirely different location. If this new computer is the first time you installed Thunderbird from Windows App Store... Personally, I would uninstall it and get download from the link because a lot of help etc information regarding profiles only refers to where Thunderbird would have the profiles stored by default. It's also easier to find.

If you downloaded the Thunderbird app from the 'Windows app Store' then your 'Thunderbird' folder containing profile will be in this location: C:\Users\username\AppData\Local\packages\MozillaThunderbird.MZLA_h5892qc0xkpca\LocalCache\Roaming\Thunderbird

content:
Please note: If you choose to upload all your Pop account emails back onto the server, it will use server quota.

IMAP is not the same as Pop. As you have used Pop previously I thought I'd add some basic info about imap.

POP Pop Account accesses only server Inbox and downloads whatever it has not previously downloaded to the pop account Inbox. There is no synchronisation between any pop folder and server folder. Pop accounts cannot access any other folder on the server. All downloaded emails are stored on your computer and they are an independent copy. You can delete emails off the server via webmail to create space and it will not effect anything in a POP account.

IMAP Imap accounts can only display whatever is on the server. Imap account folders synchronise with server folders of same name. Imap is like a mirror copy of whatever is on the server. Emails are stored on the server. You can choose to download full copies or only headers if you need to save space on computer. If you download full copies of emails, you should not regard them as independent copies because the folders synchronise with server. You can download full copies and then use it to create a backup of the Thunderbird folder containing profile data saved to another external hard drive so you do have an independent copy. As Imap accounts have emails stored on server, it means you can access the same data from other computers or phone via Imap. Anything you delete off server via webmail account or any other device will be auto deleted from an Imap account when it synchronises with server.

If you need to increase quota on server, then you can download full copies of emails and use 'COPY TO' option to save independent copies in the 'Local Folders' account before deleting the originals off the server.

I use both Pop and IMAP for different accounts. Both work perfectly ok.

Do you need more help with getting a complete copy of the Thunderbird folder on old computer putting onto the new computer ?

If no and you are ok then the next bit assumes you have already copied the 'Thunderbird' folder containing all the profile etc data to new computer.

If I were you, I would not be trying to upload all those emails back onto the server. It just takes a lot of time as servers have limits on imap uploads and it will also use up quota. You may end up having to get it back off the server to create some space.

I would also do the following to get them into the Local Folders mail account. Why ? Because it's a lot quicker when you have a lot of folders and emails.

Exit Thunderbird - this is important

  • In windows search type: %Appdata% - see image below as guide
  • Select %Appdata% file folder
  • Select Roaming
  • Select Thunderbird
  • Select Profiles
  • Select the profile name folder
  • Access Profile name folder
  • Click on 'Mail' folder
  • Right click on 'Local Folders' folder and select to open in a new window and put it to one side ready for incoming files.
  • Back in the Mail folder, click on the pop account name folder to see contents.

Assuming you do not already store anything in the Local Folders folder All the following files and folders need to be copied from the pop mail account folder and pasted into the 'Local Folders' folder. If you do have some emails stored in the Local Folders, then when you copy from pop to Local Folders, just make sure to not overwrite anything if the file name happens to be the same. Allow it to add a number to the name. You can always rename a folder later.

  • Any folder with a .sbd extension
  • Any mbox file - they do not have any extension

I've also posted an example image to act as a guide showing a copy of all mbox files and all folders with .sbd in a Pop account into the Local Folders.

When you start Thunderbird, all your folders and emails that were in the pop account are now in the Local Folders account.

content:
You can install Thunderbird on the new computer, then copy your Profile from the old to the new, which will carry over all your email data, folders, passwords, filters, everything to the new. We can advise you on how to do that. Once that's done and working you can go on to the next step, which is "converting" from POP to IMAP. It's in quotes because its not really a conversion - you have to set up a new IMAP account in parallel to the POP account.

Here's an article about "converting" from POP to IMAP:

Switch from POP to IMAP account https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/switch-pop-imap-account

A big decision for you will be whether you want all of your local POP folders to be accessible on the IMAP server. If so, you will have to manually recreate those folders and upload your local messages to those new IMAP folders. This can be tedious and doesn't always work well, depending on the host system. If you're content for those messages to remain local, you can simply move those folders to Local Folders. Eventually, when everything is working the way you like you can delete the now-unused POP account.

As for filters, there's no automated way to to that. The file "msgFilterRules.dat" is plain text and can be edited with a text editor like Windows Notepad. You can try copying the file from the POP account folder in your Profile to the new IMAP account folder and changing the destination folder names to the new ones. This could also be tedious and prone to error, but maybe or maybe not easier than recreating the filters from scratch.

content:
Lösung:

1. Wo wir uns einklinken — about:3pane statt nur messenger.xhtml

Die eigentliche Mail-Oberfläche (Ordnerbaum, Nachrichtenliste) läuft seit TB 115 in about:3pane, einem eingebetteten <browser>-Rahmen. Dort müssen wir hin.

2. Wie wir da hinkommen — gTabmail.currentAbout3Pane

Das war die eigentliche Hürde. ExtensionSupport.registerWindowListener sieht nur echte Fenster, und about:3pane ist keins. Der offizielle Weg aus der Thunderbird-Migrationsdoku:


implementation.js Ln 177–232 _install3PaneCaptureHandler(frameWin) { 

 // ...

}, _injectIntoAllAbout3Panes(outerWin) { 

 try {    // Weg 1: gTabmail.currentAbout3Pane – offizieller TB-API-Weg    if (outerWin.gTabmail && outerWin.gTabmail.currentAbout3Pane) {      this._install3PaneCaptureHandler(outerWin.gTabmail.currentAbout3Pane);    }    // Weg 2: alle tabInfo-Einträge (auch nicht-aktive Tabs)    // ...  }

}, Dazu TabOpen/TabSelect-Listener, damit auch später geöffnete Tabs erfasst werden.

3. Wann im Event-Flow — Capture- statt Bubble-Phase

Mousetrap registriert sich immer in der Bubble-Phase und ist damit zu spät. Der neue Handler nutzt die Capture-Phase und läuft dadurch garantiert vor Thunderbirds eigenen Handlern:


implementation.js Ln 196–203 

 e.preventDefault();  e.stopImmediatePropagation();  if (command !== "unset") {    executeCommand(frameWin, command);  }

}; frameWin.document.addEventListener("keydown", captureHandler, true /* capture */); stopImmediatePropagation() sorgt dafür, dass Thunderbird die Taste danach gar nicht mehr zu sehen bekommt.

Nebeneffekt Weil Mousetrap zwingend in der Bubble-Phase arbeitet, konnten wir es in about:3pane nicht verwenden. Dort läuft jetzt eigener Code: buildComboString() übersetzt das KeyboardEvent in einen Mousetrap-kompatiblen String ("a", "ctrl+shift+f"), executeCommand() führt aus. In messenger.xhtml bleibt Mousetrap unverändert als Fallback — dieselbe keys-Map, zwei Ausführungswege.

I found the solution!

It was due to a filter rule that had an additional matching rule underneath the main one. (And no, I have no idea how it got there—I don't remember doing anything with my filter rule list in ages). This additional matching rule (as you can see from the picture) had a blank filter condition where an email address or domain name would normally be entered, which meant that ANY email coming from ANYONE would be sent to my Spam folder.

Deleting that additional matching rule fixed the problem.

When I reviewed my filter rules, the list displayed did not show the additional matching rule for this entry. I have 80 filter rules and this particular rule was number 78 on the list. I started my quest by disabling all of the rules and then sending myself an email from my secondary email address. That email went to my Inbox. OK, so now I knew it was a filter problem—but which one? I then re-enabled the first 20 filter rules and sent a second TEST email. That one also went to my Inbox. I kept doing that until the TEST message went to my Spam folder instead of my Inbox. I then re-enabled that batch of rules one by one until I had narrowed it down to the one I wound up editing.

re :we are not getting the emails to our iPhones until we get out of Thunderbird.

Thunderbird program on your computer has no control over the iphone connectivity to a server.

What type of mail account have you set up in the desktop/laptop Thunderbird? Is it IMAP or POP ?

What type of mail account is set up on the iphone? Is it IMAP or POP ?

What server are you connecting to ? such as gmail, comcast, bt, yahoo etc ?

Possible idea worth checking: It could be you have used up too many cached connections when using Thunderbird, but when you exit Thunderbird those cached connections get released and so you can then connect using the iphone. The server controls the total number of allowed cached connections. The server says total number number of cached connections is not just one device it's all of them together. You can lower the number of cached connections used in Thunderbird to see if auto shutting some helps, but usually the problem is the other way around, Thunderbird gets the problem of access due to too many cached connections and the fault is often the iphone using them. In those cases switching off the iphone helps to close some connections. Is your wife also accessing the same account as that would increase the cached connections used?

cached connections are the number of connections concurrently accessing the server mail account. Imap accounts may have several folders synchronising, downloading mail etc and each is a separate connection. If you have other computes and devices doing likewise then you are using more connections. So if you have left another computer or laptop or tablet or phone etc running a connection via Outlook or Thunderbird or any email client, then they are all using cached connections.

You could try to restrict cached connections in Thunderbird if you are using IMAP to see if it helps. If using IMAP then check this: In Thunderbird

  • Account Settings > Server Settings for the account
  • Click on 'Advanced' button
  • 'Maximum number of server connections to cache' default is set at 5
  • suggest you try '3'
  • Note do not increase more then 5.
  • Click on 'OK'

re :Just to help clarify, here's the location of the old folders as per the "properties" info. mailbox:///E:/thunderbird data/thunderbird/yetudx3p.default/Mail/Local Folders/Friends & family

OK, so it looks like you moved the 'profile name folder called 'yetudx3p.default' onto the E Drive.

You are talking about the 'Local Folders' account. That is not a Pop account nor an imap account.

The folders in that account listed at the top seem to be unusual - messed up - it has a load of default folders in the 'Archives' folder such as 'Outbox', 'Junk', and 'Trash'. None of them should be in the 'Archives' folder. Move them back out of the 'Archives' folder - you have to drag and drop them into the account name at the top in order to put them in the proper location.

'Outbox' is a folder usually located in 'Local Folders' and it's used by all mail accounts when using 'Send Later'.

So I'm wondering - Did you rename the 'Local Folders' account to say your email address ? I have a suspicion that that account at the top is really your 'Local Folders' account. Do this:

  • In 'Account Settings'
  • Select the name of that old proton email address account name.
  • Look on the right side - what does it say ?
  • Does it 'The following is a special account....'
  • If yes, then that is your Local Folders' account.
  • Where it says 'Account Name' - remove all content and type 'Local Folders'

That will stop all the confusion over account names and it will also match local directory name. So from now onwards I'm calling that top old account 'Local Folders'.

If I'm right and it was the 'Local Folders' account just been misnamed then all of those emails are stored on your computer and they do not synchronise with any server. They are an independent copy of emails on your computer.

I would recommend that you leave all of those folders alone because you can still see all the emails.

Regarding the new account. That is an imap account and it can only display whatever is on he server. So emails are stored on the server and you are getting a mirror like view of the server. You should not consider any imap folder as being a true independent copy on your computer. If the emails are fully downloaded then it can be used to create a backup which you store on an external drive. However, because all imap folders synchronise with server they are not a true independent copy on computer.

If you want to get all those emails stored in all those various folders that are currently in the 'Local Folders' account uploaded back onto the server in order to see them in the imap account, then please note, it will decrease your available quota on the server, so you may end up having to get them back off the server again. You would need to create folders in the imap account in order to receive them. You would then need to highlight a batch of emails, use right click 'Copy To' and select the imap folder you created. Please note uploading emails via imap back onto a server is not a quick exercise. You would need to find out what limitations are set by the server. You may find you can only upload X per hour or daily. Personally, I would not bother unless you use more than one computer in different locations and really need to see all those emails currently in 'Local Folders'.

Perhaps you would like to rearrange the position of the accounts in the Folder Pane. Maybe you would like the new imap protonmail account to be at the top, If yes:

  • In 'Account Settings'
  • In the Left Pane
  • Left click and hold down the name of the new imap protonmail account and drag it up above the 'Local Folders' account/old account.

This will then rearrange the Folder Pane.

content:
Thunderbird is an email client - a program running on your computer and it does not need a password in order to run.

I think you maybe talking about a mail account password for a specific email address.

All passwords are created and modified only in the webmail account for the email address. Your wife would need to use a browser such as Firefox or Edge to directly logon to the webmail account for her email address. It would ask for username which is usually the email address and a password. If your wife cannot remember the password, there is usually a link - something like 'Forgotten Password' which she would have to use and follow instructions to regain access to the webmail account. Once she has access to the webmail account, then she needs to reset the password.

Once the new password has been set up, then you use that in Thunderbird to set up the mail account.

If the account is already set up and you need to update the stored password:

  • Settings > Privacy & Security
  • scroll to Passwords section
  • click on 'Saved Passwords'
  • click on 'Show Passwords'

If you get asked by Windows Security in a small window for a password or pin: When you start computer and enter password to access the computer User Account, that is the password required to access 'Show Passwords'.

If you get asked by Thunderbird for the 'Primary Password', that means this is a separate password set up to prevent users of the same computer from seeing her stored password. Your wife would need to enter that password - note this is not a mail account password and it should have been a unique password only your wife would know about. If that 'Primary Password' has been forgotten then I can supply info on how to get it set back to no password, but in doing so, all stored passwords will be erased because it is a security setting to protect stored passwords.

Once access to 'Show Passwords' has been obtained: The mail account will have two lines for the account an incoming and an outgoing, so both of those lines need fixing. Note - if the account was set up using Authentication Method OAuth2 then you would only see one oauth line - you cannot edit that password token as it is set up automatically.

  • Right click on each line in turn and select 'Edit Password'
  • completely clear the password, then type in new password.
  • click on 'Close'

Exit Thunderbird wait a few moments for the background processes to complete - it just makes sure all data is properly saved. Restart Thunderbird.

If this info helps you then please select this comment as a 'Chosen Solution'

If you need further info on this, that's ok, just ask :)

re :The Saved Logins window is blank (see attachment). I also grabbed a screenshot of the Privacy and Security page section for Passwords as there is a checkbox there to "require device signin to fill and manage passwords."

That means if you want to see and edit etc your Saved Passwords, do you want an additional layer of security to force a request for password to see those stored passwords. If it is selected then when you click on 'Show Passwords', a Windows Security window pops up asking for a specific password - when you boot up computer and get asked to enter a password in order to log on to your computer User Account desktop - it wants that password.

If a 'Primary Password' is set up, then Thunderbird would ask for that Primary Password. The Primary Password option is designed to stop prying eyes getting access to stored password, it does not stop people from seeing emails etc. It is usually used by people who share the computer with others who also have access to the same computer User Account, so they know that password. The 'Primary Password' should be very unique and never a mail account password nor a computer User Account password. If a Primary Password is forgotten, then it require a reset and that means it removes the Primary Password and also every stored password, because it is a security issue - anyone can follow instructions to clear a Primary Password, so you would not like them to clear it and access stored passwords.

In your case, it has no effect on the issue of not connecting with server. I suspect that issue is to do with a problem of the mail account password. As no passwords were saved, it seems something is wrong and needs fixing in order to rule it out. See previous comment.

content:
Hello there


You can configure this setting in the following places. Follow the steps below in this order to address the issue:


1.Check the message filters.


2.Check the junk email settings:

Right-click your email account in the left-hand column and choose Settings.

Under the account name, click Junk.

On the right-hand side, under the heading "Destination and Retention," check where junk messages are being moved. Is this accidentally set to the Trash folder instead of the Junk folder?

If the folder is correct, but all email is still being treated as spam, temporarily uncheck the option "Enable adaptive junk mail controls for this account" to test if the behavior stops.


3.Check for synchronisation conflicts with other devices (POP and IMAP):

The POP issue: If another device connects via the POP protocol and is set to delete messages from the server after downloading, the server's inbox will be emptied.

The result in Thunderbird: Because Thunderbird works via IMAP, the program sees that the server inbox is empty and that the mail on the server has been moved to the trash.

Thunderbird synchronises this immediately and moves the mail to the local trash folder as well.

Solution: Check the mail settings on your devices and ensure they are either set to IMAP or that the option "Leave messages on the server" is enabled.


4.Check webmail for these errors. 5.Repair corrupted folder indexes .

The system of incoming email consolidation and aggregation of outgoing mail you describe is, in my perception, not the way the vast majority of average and even above average users are using the email ecosystem. If users are experiencing poor email service they don't consider it's the incoming or outgoing server that is causing the issue. It's just this service is poor, I need to move to a better provider. Users treat the incoming and outgoing services as inseparable. Thunderbird Google kontakty ignoruje jen částečně. Google kontakty lze v současných verzích Thunderbirdu synchronizovat přímo pomocí CardDAV, takže kvůli samotným kontaktům už není nutný doplněk. Problém jsou ale právě skupiny (štítky) v Google Kontaktech – nativní CardDAV podpora Thunderbirdu je nepřenáší.

Pro synchronizaci Google kontaktů včetně skupin tedy stále potřebujete doplněk, například Google-4-TbSync nebo CardBook. Google-4-TbSync je přímo určený pro synchronizaci kontaktů a skupin pomocí Google People API.

A právě tady je problém s „trvalým“ řešením: doplňky tohoto typu používají rozhraní Thunderbirdu, která se při velkých změnách TB mohou měnit. Oficiální Thunderbird Extension Finder proto u TbSync a CardBook doporučuje spíše Thunderbird ESR, protože mezi jeho aktualizacemi jsou změny rozhraní méně časté.

Takže pokud jsou pro vás Google skupiny zásadní, za nejrozumnější dlouhodobé řešení bych považoval Thunderbird ESR + CardBook/TbSync, nikoli běžnou (rapid) verzi Thunderbirdu.

content:
Assuming the messages you want to copy to the new computer were either from a POP3 account or/and Local folders, I would copy those files from the old computer to the new and import them using the add-on "ImportExportTools NG" (https://addons.thunderbird.net/en-US/thunderbird/addon/importexporttools-ng/).

- On the travel computer, start Thunderbird, go to <Help | Troubleshooting Information | Profile Folder> and click the "Open Folder" button.

- Close Thunderbird.

- You want to copy the entire "Mail" folder to the new computer. You can copy that folder to a transfer device like a thumb drive.

- On the target computer, copy the "Mail" folder to a convenient temporary location (Desktop?)

- (Note that when you examine the contents of the Mail folder, you will see several sub-folders, each representing a POP3 account, plus one called "Local Folders.)

- In Thunderbird on the target computer, create a new Local Folder called "Imported Mail" (or whatever you want.)

- Right-click on that folder and choose <ImportExportTools NG | IMport mbox files | All mbox files from directory (with sbd structure>. Navigate to and enter the temporary folder on Windows Desktop you created earlier.

- Select one of the folders you wish to import and click Select Folder. The folder and its contents will now import into your current Thunderbird local folder.

- Repeat the last two steps for every folder you want to import.

You will now have all your old POP and Local Folders in your current Thunderbird profile's Local Folders where they can be organized to your liking.

content:
Thank you for your excellent screen shot! It proves that your "old" prefs.js file with a size of 64 kB has been renamed in "invalidprefs.js" for an unknown reason (most times this is caused by a crash or a power outage), whilst a new virgin prefs.js of 7 kB size has been created automatically. So the culprit for the loss of your accounts is known. The good news is that accounts and messages are still stored in your profile folder.

How solve this problem? If you have a recent backup of your profile folder make a copy of the prefs.js file in the backup and replace the prefs.js file in your actual profile folder with the 64 kB copy. You must exit Thunderbird before the replacement. Probably you have no backup, so go back in your profile folder, exit Thunderbird, remove the 7 bB prefs.js file and rename "invalidprefs.js" in prefs.js Then restart Thunderbird and report back.

If your old prefs.js file is really corrupted, renaming the "invalidprefs.js" won't work and you'll have to recreate all your accounts manually. If you have been using the IMAP protocol you'll automatically retrieve your folders and messages. If you have been using the POP protocol and/or the Local Folders to store messages it will be a bit more complicated to retrieve folders and messages, but I'll direct you until you got them back.

So I presume that your prefs.js file in the Thunderbird profile has been damaged for an unknown reason and renamed in prefs-1.js oder invalidprefs.js. At the same time Thunderbird has created a new pristine prefs.js file of a 6 to 7 kB size which doesn't contain any account setiings. This is the reason why your Thunderbird window displays an empty folder pane, and probably your Account Settings tab is empty, too.

Please go to Help > Troubleshooting Information > Profile Folder > Open Folder, then exit Thunderbird. In the profile folder search for a prefs.js file and retrieve its size. Also look for a (bigger) prefs-1.js (or invalidprefs.js) file with a an actual time stamp.

content:
To connect to a Yahoo server, I would advise you do the following first.

Firewall The Firewall on your computer may be controlled by the OS by default OR it might be controlled by an Anti-Virus you installed. Access the Firewall and set up the Thunderbird program as an allowed program. This will ensure nothing is blocking Thunderbird.

VPN Check you computer for a VPN. Many server do not like VPN because they hide your IP address, so server wonders if you a hacker trying to access the account, so might block access. Many Anti-Virus products now include a VPN, so check it out and switch it off.

In Thunderbird Yahoo uses something called 'Oauth2' for it's Authentication Method. When you create the mail account, you will find that Thunderbird will automatically look for correct server settings and set up for an Imap account. So if you want POP, that is the time to select a different protocol.

To use Oauth some settings need to be set up.

  • In 'Settings' > 'Privacy & Security'
  • Under 'Web Content' section
  • Select 'Accept cookies from sites'
  • Accept third party cookies 'Always'

This required because during creation of mail account, you will find a new tab will open in your browser, it may ask for email address and password and it will be Yahoo basically saying do you want to allow Thunderbird access to server. Obviously the answer is yes, Thunderbird needs to be allowed. Then Yahoo set up Oauth token which gets auto saved in Thunderbird in the same place as stored Passwords. Thunderbird will use automatically when needing to connect to server to get emails.

content:
Thunderbird program is an email client. You create a mail account for an existing email address. You appear to have an email address because you mention 'from my yahoo email account'.

You can set up a POP account or an Imap Mail account. POP accounts can only access the server and download emails from the server Inbox to the Pop account Inbox. If you want to keep copies of messages on server, then in 'Account Settings' > 'Server Settings' for the Pop account, you need to select 'Leave messages on server', otherwise they get removed off the server. Pop accounts cannot access any other server folder. If you have emails in other server folders maybe some you created, then after downloading emails from the Inbox, you would have to logon to the yahoo webmail account and move emails from other fodler into the Ibox and then in Thunderbird click on 'Get Messages to download them to your Inbox. Create a suitable folder name in the Pop account and then move those emails into that folder.

All folders in a POP account are completely independent copies on your computer because there is no synchronising with the server folders.

IMAP accounts work differently. All imap account folders synchronise with server folders of same name. Imap account folders can only display whatever is on the server. So it is like a mirror copy. If you delete anything off the server via the webmail yahoo account, when folders synchronise those deleted emails will get deleted from the imap account. You can download full copies of emails, but you should not consider them to be an independent copy because all folders synchronise with server. However, you can use the imap account to create a backup AND you can also right click on emails and select 'Copy to' and select a suitable folder in the 'Local Folders' account.

The 'Local Folders' account is a special account created by Thunderbird and anything stored in that account is completely independent of the server, there is no synchronising with the server and like a Pop account all emails are stored on your computer.

Many people set up an Imap account and then get copies of important emails put into the 'Local Folders' account. The Local Folders' account is also useful if you find you need to create some space on the server to increase your quota. You can get copies of emails into the 'Local Folders' account before you delete them from the imap account folders, which would remove them off the server when folder synchronises with server.

I will summarize for you so you are not in the dark. Remove Norton and remove the problem. That is all. Or you can change the settings as was first suggested to you by Ed. This is not really a Thunderbird problem, despite the symptom appearing in Thunderbird.

Now to digress a little. You think it important to scan incoming messages. Microsoft apparently does not! They built an antivirus product that tests in the top tier at each antivirus test it is included in and is the number one end point product in the corporate world. Yet it ignores email entirely. Consider that before making assumptions about what is "necessary" I approached Symantec probably 15 years ago and asked them what was the purpose of email scanning. Their answer was "another line of defense". Putting sewerage in the moat is also another line of defense. However most of us dispensed with the moat centuries ago for defense and I do not know if the sewerage did much more than make the place small bad. . Personally I dispensed with antivirus scanning of email years ago and am untroubled with attacks from email. But I use Gmail and other top tier mail providers that provide malware scanning with their service. I also allow defender unrestrained access to my system,

So some things about antivirus products that frequently affect receiving mail and therefore Thunderbird.

  • Scanning of encrypted connections. (Norton not Defender)
  • Scanning of email (Norton and a host of paid antivirus products offering "another line of defense" not Defender)
  • VPN (Norton and host of paid antivirus products trying to make themselves relevant offering a product way outside of the malware arena, not defender)
  • Scanning in Thunderbird's profile folder. I think they all do this differently, but mostly unsuccessfully. Thunderbird maintains a lot of very large files. Often in the gigabyte range size wise. This takes quite a lot of time to scan when they are changed (think deleting an email, moving one or send one or even getting one.) What happens when scanning is occurring when Thunderbird tries to update a file is technically called file contention and like when you try and share a car parking space with another car the outcome is not good. Your experience is Thunderbird unable to access it's data and complaining about it.

To make Thunderbird lest prone of failure to access it's data you have to disable any form of scanning of the file in Thunderbird profile folder by the antivirus when they are accessed. Norton makes this hard as you have to exclude multiple sub folders as Thunderbird profile is a folder tree and Norton apparently can only comprehend one file of folder at a time, not a branch of a tree.

Anti-virus software is often the culprit when Thunderbird is not responding. Specifically ESET has been known to cause problems with Thunderbird. https://wiki.mozilla.org/Thunderbird:Testing:Antivirus_Related_Performance_Issues#ESET

Don't let your anti-virus software scan attachments.

Don't let your anti-virus software intercept your secure connection to the server.

Remove any add-ons your anti-virus software may have installed in Thunderbird.

Keep it working. https://kb.mozillazine.org/Keep_it_working_-_Thunderbird

And last but not least, backup your Thunderbird profile on a regular basis. https://support.mozilla.org/kb/profiles-where-thunderbird-stores-user-data#w_backing-up-a-profile

I can't use the trendy phrase TLDR (Too Long Didn't Read), but you're very verbose and I'm having trouble picking the essential issues out of your post. But I'll make some comments:

- According to this support article <https://help.yahoo.com/kb/SLN37064.html>, basic Yahoo service has a storage size limit of 20 GB, regardless of how many messages there are. You can pay extra for more space.

- Thunderbird has no practical limit on number or size of messages or folders. The only limits are those imposed by the email provider, and possibly local file system limits in older operating systems.

- If you're running up against Yahoo's limit, rather than relying on some unsupported hack like the "export" thing, maybe you should consider alternatives like transferring some of those messages to a second account. Or moving some messages to Local Folders in Thunderbird, thus taking some pressure off your Yahoo/ATT account. The only reason to keep all those thousands of messages on the server is so they are always accessible on multiple devices. That would be a valid reason, of course, but it is really necessary for you?

- Your Thunderbird Profile is where all your messages, folders, preferences, filters, passwords, etc. are stored. It's separate and distinct from the actual program. You can find its location by going to <Help | Troubleshooting Information | Profiles | about:profiles | Default Profile | Root Directory>. Clicking the Open Folder button will open your operating system's file browser in your Profile folder. In Windows, the default location is:

"C:\Users\(Windows account)\AppData\Roaming\Thunderbird\Profiles\(Thunderbird Profile)"

You can make a backup copy of this folder (while Thunderbird is closed) and restore it if ever something goes wrong. Actually, you should make regular backups of this folder if your email is precious to you.

It's easiest to delete any Saved Passwords for that account in <Settings | Privacy & Security | Passwords | Saved Passwords>. Then restart Thunderbird, and you should be asked for your credentials.

If you use OAuth2, a browser window will open where you can enter your user ID and password. You must have cookies allowed in Thunderbird for this to work. If you use Normal Password, depending on your provider, you may need to create and use an "application password", which would be distinct from your regular log-in password.

content:
The 'undeliverable' message usually contains a more information which can help detect the cause. Here's a list of some common reasons which your dad and brother need to check out:

  • If the sent emails are failing the server spam filter then they will be undeliverable.
  • If the receiving server is full, person has used quota, then server cannot receive the email and is returned as undeliverable.
  • If the sender has sent to an email address that has a typo, in other words it's not correct and therefore does not exist, then the email will be returned as undeliverable.

You also did not mention whether they only have a problem sending emails to you or whether they have a problem sending any email.

If they have a problem only sending to you: You can check to see how much server quota you have used. If it's nearly full, there may be occasions when it is full until you delete some emails then there is a small space to receive again. So it might be an intermittent issue. If your server quota is nearly full then delete old emails off the server. If you need copies of them then get copies into Local Folders' account first before you delete anything.

You could also logon to your webmail account and make sure there is no filter that is blocking those senders.

Dad and brother need to check they have got the correct email address. Check carefully for typos etc. They also need to find out whether the undeliverable message mentions spam. It could be they have send a message that has a lot of links or remote content or uses words that the server might think it's spam. If they have a general problem with sending, it's possible they are sending using an IP address or email address which has been flagged as sending spam so it's blocked. They could use spamhaus to check. https://check.spamhaus.org/
